text: Bounds checking costs a comparison on every access. Why is the real cost usually near zero?
choices: Branch prediction handles it, and the JIT eliminates checks the loop condition already proves safe
Modern processors have a dedicated bounds instruction
The cost is not near zero; it is substantial
The check is performed only in debug builds
explanation: In for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++), the condition already guarantees i is in range, so the compiler removes the per-access check. Writing the ordinary obvious loop lets the optimizer help; a clever hand-optimized version often defeats it.
